data.title: Singapore Stocks Edge Higher As Banks Offset Regional Weakness
data.description:
Singapore shares eked out a modest gain on Sept 11, bucking a broader regional sell-off as strength in heavyweight banks helped offset cautious sentiment fuelled by elevated oil prices and Middle East tensions.

The Straits Times Index (STI) rose 0.08% to 5,694.02 points, even as most major Asian markets finished lower. Surging crude prices during the week had revived inflation concerns and pressured risk appetite across the region.

Banking stocks provided support to the local benchmark. OCBC and UOB gained about 0.7% each, while DBS added 0.3%, helping Singapore outperform regional peers including Japan, South Korea, Hong Kong and Malaysia.

Elsewhere among blue chips, DFI Retail Group fell 3.1%, making it one of the STI’s weakest performers.

Market breadth remained cautious despite the benchmark’s gain, with 340 declining counters versus 215 advancers. About 1.1 billion securities worth S$1.5 billion changed hands.

Investors remained focused on oil prices and inflation risks, with Brent crude staying above US$100 a barrel amid disruptions and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, raising concerns over the outlook for global interest rates.

data.title: Wall Street Rallies As Oil Retreats, Rate-Hike Bets Surge
data.description:
Wall Street closed sharply higher on Sept 11 as easing oil prices and hotter US inflation data strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise interest rates at its policy meeting next week.

According to Reuters, the S&P 500 climbed 0.86% to 7,656.98, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.96% to 26,333.04. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.98% to 52,573.29.

US consumer prices accelerated last month as gasoline costs rebounded, adding pressure on the Fed to keep inflation in check. Interest-rate futures now price in nearly a 90% probability of a rate hike on Wednesday, up from 72% a day earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Technology and artificial intelligence-linked hardware stocks were among the session’s strongest performers. Dell surged 12% to a record high, Hewlett Packard Enterprise jumped 12% and HP gained 8.4% following stronger-than-expected quarterly results from Oracle. Oracle itself slipped 1.8%.

Nine of the S&P 500’s 11 sectors advanced, led by communication services, which gained 1.35%, followed by consumer discretionary with a 1.13% rise.

Investor sentiment was also helped by lower oil prices. Brent crude fell nearly 3%, although it remained above US$104 a barrel and was still up around 9% for the week amid concerns over disruptions along Middle Eastern shipping routes.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell two points to 15.88, signalling easing market anxiety.

Despite the rebound, the S&P 500 lost 0.8% for the week while the Nasdaq declined 0.7%. The benchmark remains roughly 2% below its Aug 13 record close but is still up about 12% so far in 2026.

data.title: US Stocks Rise As CPI Remains Sticky, Indexes Up 1%
data.description:
US stocks rose on Friday as investors digested the Consumer Price Index data, which showed inflation remained sticky and cemented bets that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates next week.

The Dow Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite each climbed roughly 1%. The move comes after those indexes have faced a four-day losing streak.

Investors turned their attention to the Consumer Price Index, the last piece of inflation data before Federal Reserve policymakers convene next week. Overall prices rose 0.4% on a monthly basis and 3.4% on an annual basis, which were in line with economists’ expectations and slightly hotter than July’s reading.

While inflation has trended lower since May, it remains well above the Fed’s 2% goal. The recent spike in oil prices has only fueled inflation concerns after Brent crude prices topped $108 per barrel before easing back on Friday and diesel reached its highest price ever, at $6 per gallon.

The increase in oil prices, as well as Friday’s CPI report, prompted traders to ramp up their bets that the Fed will raise interest rates this month. Markets are now pricing in a roughly 86% chance the Fed raises interest rates by 25 basis points at the FOMC meeting next week, according to the CME’s Fedwatch tool. That’s up from 72% a day ago and 50% a week ago.

data.title: High Oil Prices Drag Bursa Lower
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia closed sharply lower on Sept 11, tracking another round of regional selling as persistently high crude oil prices continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

At the closing bell, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 18.78 points, or 1.1%, to 1,686.74 from previous day’s close of 1,705.52. The benchmark traded between 1,682.56 and 1,705.69 during the session.

Losses were broad-based, with the FBM 70 dropped 171.96 points, or 0.96%, to 17,728.64, while the F4GBM declined 11.23 points, or 1.1%, to 1,014.23.

The FBM Emas slipped 128.95 points, or 1.02%, to 12,510.20, while the FBM Shariah lost 105.89 points, or 0.85%, to 12,396.81.

Among the most actively traded stocks, Top Glove Corporation Bhd gained 3.5 sen to 80 sen on about 210.5 million shares, while Zetrix AI Bhd was unchanged at 25 sen on 182.4 million shares.

Supermax Corporation Bhd fell one sen to 42 sen on 64.4 million shares, while GTA Holdings Bhd advanced 2.5 sen to 35.5 sen on 57.4 million shares. Luster Industries Bhd was unchanged at 3.5 sen on 54.2 million shares.

Total market turnover stood at 3.57 billion units worth RM3.28 billion compared to 3.98 billion units valued at RM3.14 billion on Sept 10.

The weaker close capped a cautious session for Malaysian equities, with elevated crude oil prices continuing to pressure risk appetite across regional markets.

data.title: Allianz, Hong Leong Bank Lead Bursa Losers As Selling Pressure Dominates
data.description:

Allianz was the top loser, sliding 56 sen to RM21.12, followed by Hong Leong Bank, which fell 52 sen to RM23.08. Sunway Construction Group Bhd dropped 47 sen to RM7.44, while Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd lost 44 sen to RM23.56 and ViTrox Corp Bhd declined 32 sen to RM9.15.

On the upside, Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd topped the list, rising 27 sen to RM5.09. Eurospan Holdings Bhd advanced 18 sen to RM3.15, while Batu Kawan Bhd and Concrete Engineering Products Bhd each added 12 sen, closing at RM20.16 and RM4 respectively.

Mega Fortris Bhd rounded out the top five gainers, climbing nine sen to RM2.40.

Total market turnover stood at 3.57 billion units worth RM3.28 billion compared to 3.98 billion units valued at RM3.14 billion on Sept 10.

data.title: Tokyo Stocks End Lower On Oil Prices, Rising Bond Yields
data.description:
Tokyo stocks ended lower Friday, with the Nikkei index briefly plunging over 3 percent, as crude oil prices climbed, while rising bond yields also fueled inflation concerns.

The benchmark Nikkei stock index, the 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average, ended down 1,259.61 points, or 1.93 percent, from Thursday at 64,011.34.

The broader Topix index, meanwhile, finished 26.28 points, or 0.65 percent, lower at 4,028.30.

Due to escalating Middle East supply concerns, the benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures price has climbed above the psychologically significant mark of 100 U.S. dollars per barrel for the first time since mid-May, analysts said.

Meanwhile, the yield on the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond rose to 3 percent at one stage, also weighing on sentiment in the Tokyo stock market.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Slightly Lower At Midday As Oil Surge, US-Iran Tensions Hit Sentiment
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia extended its decline at midday of Sept 11, tracking weaker regional markets as surging oil prices and ongoing US-Iran tensions pressured heavyweight counters.

At 12.30 pm, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 17.18 points, or 1%, to 1,688.34 from its morning opening of 1,705.29, after trading between 1,687.44 and 1,705.69.

The broader market was similarly weaker, the FBM 70 dropped 143.90 points, or 0.8%, to 17,756.70, while the F4GBM slid 10.08 points, or 0.98%, to 1,015.38. The FBM Emas declined 114.41 points, or 0.91%, to 12,524.74, while the FBM Shariah lost 105.56 points, or 0.84%, to 12,397.14.

Market breadth remained firmly negative, with 744 decliners outpacing 336 gainers. Another 417 counters were unchanged, 1,334 untraded and 32 suspended.

Among the biggest losers, Allianz Malaysia Bhd fell 40 sen to RM21.28, Sunway Construction Group Bhd dropped 33 sen to RM7.58 and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd declined 32 sen to RM22.42. Hong Leong Bank Bhd slipped 30 sen to RM23.30, while IHH Healthcare Bhd lost 29 sen to RM7.60.

Energy-linked counters bucked the weaker market, with Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd leading the gainers, rising 24 sen to RM5.06, followed by Hengyuan Refining Co Bhd up 13 sen to RM3.52. Concrete Engineering Products Bhd gained 12 sen to RM4, Eurospan Holdings Bhd advanced 10 sen to RM3.07 and Hartalega Holdings Bhd climbed eight sen to RM1.19.

On the other hand, Top Glove Corporation Bhd was the most actively traded counter, gaining four sen to 80.5 sen on volume of about 143.65 million shares, followed by Zetrix AI Bhd, which edged up half a sen to 25.5 sen on 114.1 million shares, while Luster Industries Bhd was unchanged at 3.5 sen on 53.48 million shares. Supermax Corporation Bhd was flat at 43 sen on 51.16 million shares, while Hartalega rose eight sen to RM1.19 on 32.73 million shares.

Total market turnover stood at 2.22 billion shares worth RM1.58 billion by the midday break.

data.title: Stock Picks: Stratus Global Holdings Bhd And Hibiscus Petroleum Bhd
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified Stratus Global Holdings Bhd and Hibiscus Petroleum Bhd as trading picks, with both counters showing bullish technical setups that could extend their recent gains.

For Stratus Global, RHB Research said the stock has moved above its 21-day simple moving average and closed above the RM2.90 resistance level, signalling a shift in its short-term trend towards the upside. If momentum holds, the research house sees the counter advancing towards RM3.05, followed by RM3.20.

The bullish view would be invalidated if Stratus Global falls below RM2.75, which RHB Research said could trigger a correction.

Meanwhile, RHB Research is also positive on Hibiscus Petroleum after the oil and gas counter broke above RM2.25 resistance on strong price action. The breakout, accompanied by a bullish candlestick, points to renewed upside momentum, with the next resistance levels seen at RM2.40 and RM2.55.

For Hibiscus, RHB Research identified RM2.10 as the key support level, warning that a break below this threshold could signal fading momentum and the start of a correction.

The latest technical setups put both stocks on RHB Research’s trading radar, with Stratus Global offering a rebound play above RM2.90 and Hibiscus Petroleum building on its breakout above RM2.25.

data.title: Kospi Tumbles 231.42 Points At Open As Fed Rate-Hike Fears Rattle Seoul
data.description:
South Korean shares opened sharply lower on Sept 11, with the benchmark Kospi sliding 231.42 points, or 3.29%, to 6,802.50, as investors tracked Wall Street losses and reassessed the risk of another US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

According to Yonhap, sentiment weakened after US producer prices rose 0.4% in August from the previous month, accelerating from July’s 0.1% increase and reinforcing concerns that inflation remains sticky enough to prompt tighter monetary policy.

Wall Street had already come under pressure overnight as surging oil prices and escalating Middle East tensions added to inflation worries. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.6%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite declined 0.65%.

The combination of firmer US inflation, elevated energy prices and weaker global equities weighed heavily on Seoul at the opening bell.

Investors are now awaiting the US consumer price data for further clues on the Fed’s next move, with the report likely to play a key role in shaping expectations ahead of its upcoming policy meeting.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Opens Lower As Oil Jitters, Wall Street Weakness Weigh On Sentiment
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Sept 11 as continued weakness on Wall Street, elevated crude oil prices and uncertainty surrounding the prolonged US-Iran conflict kept investors cautious.

At 9.10 am, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 3.73 points, or 0.21%, to 1,701.79, from its previous close of 1,705.52.

The broader market was also softer as the FBM 70 declined 75.46 points to 17,825.14, the FBM Emas slipped 32.19 points to 12,606.96, while the FBM Shariah eased 42.44 points to 12,460.26.

Market breadth remained negative, with 256 decliners outpacing 164 gainers, while 295 counters were unchanged.

Among the biggest losers, Sunway Construction Group Bhd fell 22 sen to RM7.69, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd dropped 20 sen to RM40.78 and ViTrox Corporation Bhd declined 12 sen to RM9.35. Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd and IHH Healthcare Bhd also traded lower.

Oil-linked counters, however, found some support amid elevated crude prices. Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd rose 13 sen to RM3.52, while Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd gained eight sen to RM4.90. Kerjaya Prospek Bhd climbed seven sen to RM3.59.

Top Glove Corporation Bhd was the most actively traded counter in the early trading as the counter rose one sen to 77.5 sen, followed by Luster Industries Bhd, Silver Ridge Holdings Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd.

Turnover stood at 283.38 million shares worth RM144.77 million in early trading.

data.title: Singapore Stocks Rebound At Open, STI Regains 5,700 On Bargain Hunting
data.description:
Singapore shares opened higher on Sept 11 with the Straits Times Index (STI) gaining 12.57 points, or 0.22%, to 5,702.32, reclaiming the psychologically important 5,700 level.

The early rebound appeared to be driven largely by bargain hunting in blue-chip stocks following its sell-off on Sept 10, when the STI dropped 0.7% to 5,689.75 as surging oil prices and escalating tensions around the Strait of Hormuz rattled investors.

Underlying sentiment towards Singapore equities also remains supported by solid corporate earnings and an improving outlook for the benchmark. Brokerages have recently raised their STI targets, with the consensus 12-month target reaching 6,140 points, reflecting optimism over earnings and Singapore’s economic resilience.

Still, gains could face resistance as investors remain cautious over the global backdrop. Brent crude has surged above US$100 a barrel, fuelling fresh inflation concerns, while higher US Treasury yields and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve (Fed) policy have pressured global equities.

Attention is now firmly on the latest US consumer inflation data, which could further shape expectations for the Fed’s policy decision next week.

data.title: HSIF Breaks Below 25,000 As Selling Pressure Accelerates
data.description:
Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) slipped below a key support level on Sept 10, with RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) saying bearish momentum is gaining traction even as it retains a positive trading bias for now.

The futures index dropped 307 points to close at 24,900 after opening at 25,200. It briefly touched 25,202 before selling pressure dragged it to an intraday low of 24,842, pushing it beneath the previous 25,000-point support.

Pressure intensified in the evening session, with HSIF falling another 199 points to 24,701. RHB noted that the Relative Strength Index was turning lower while the contract had also slipped below its 50-day simple moving average, reinforcing signs of weakening momentum.

Despite the pullback, RHB Research maintained its long position initiated at 24,657, saying the broader technical setup remains positive unless HSIF breaches the 24,600 level. The stop-loss has accordingly been set at 24,600.

The immediate support level now stands at 24,600, followed by 24,000, while resistance is pegged at 26,000 and 26,350.

With bearish momentum building, the 24,600-point level is now the key line to watch for whether HSIF’s broader bullish structure can hold.

data.title: Ringgit Retreats To 4.0680 As Strong US Data Lifts Dollar
data.description:
The ringgit opened slightly lower against the US dollar on Sept 11, easing to 4.0680/0745 as stronger-than-expected US economic data boosted demand for the greenback.

The local currency had ended Sept 10 at 4.0630/0670 against the US dollar.

Despite the softer start against the greenback, the ringgit strengthened against most major currencies.

It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.6337/6381 from 2.6431/6459, edged higher versus the euro to 4.7238/7313 from 4.7269/7315, and strengthened against the British pound to 5.4967/5055 from 5.5046/5100.

Against regional peers, the ringgit traded mixed. It firmed against the Singapore dollar to 3.2082/2136 from 3.2113/2148 and strengthened versus the Thai baht to 12.2696/2948 from 12.3331/3497.

The local note was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 231.8/232.3 from 231.5/231.8, while slipping against the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.52 from 6.49/6.50.

data.title: Wall Street Falls As Oil Surge, Fed Rate-Hike Fears Hit Tech
data.description:
US stocks closed lower on Sept 10 as surging oil prices, firm producer inflation and climbing Treasury yields revived fears that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could raise interest rates next week.

According to Reuters, the S&P 500 fell 0.58% to 7,591.75, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.65% to 26,081.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.6% to close at 52,064.10.

Oil was a major pressure point. Brent crude surged 6% to US$107 a barrel as disruptions to supply routes through the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea heightened inflation concerns amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Treasury yields also climbed sharply, with the benchmark 10-year yield reaching its highest level in nearly three years. The 30-year yield hit its highest in more than 19 years, while the two-year yield rose to its strongest level in more than two years.

Adding to the pressure, August producer prices rose in line with expectations on a monthly basis, driven partly by higher energy costs. Traders now price in a 70% probability that the Fed will raise rates by at least 25 basis points next week, up from about 64% before the report.

Technology stocks weighed on the market, with Nvidia dropping 2.3% and Micron Technology sliding 4.7%. Apple bucked the trend, jumping 3.6% a day after unveiling a US$1,999 iPhone.

Nine of the S&P 500’s 11 sectors finished lower, led by materials, which fell 1.45%, while information technology declined 0.91%.

The S&P 500 has now lost 2% over four sessions, its steepest four-day decline since June, and sits nearly 3% below its Aug 13 record closing high. The benchmark remains up about 11% for 2026.

Elsewhere, Macy’s fell 4.7% despite raising its annual outlook, while American Eagle Outfitters plunged 14% after maintaining its comparable-sales forecast amid weak discretionary spending.

Investors now turn to Sept 11’s August consumer inflation report for the next major clue on the Fed’s rate path.

data.title: Bursa Ends Lower As West Asia War, High Oil Prices Weigh On Sentiment

data.title: Tokyo Stocks Rises On AI And Semiconductor Demand
data.description:
Tokyo stocks ended higher Thursday, driven by gains in artificial intelligence- and semiconductor-related issues.

The benchmark Nikkei stock index, the 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average, ended up 128.17 points, or 0.2 percent, higher than Wednesday at 65,270.95.

The broader Topix index, meanwhile, finished 7.94 points, or 0.2 percent, higher at 4,054.58.

On the stock market, earlier losses stemming from elevated crude oil prices and the subsequent rise in bond yields were erased by gains in some AI- and chip-related shares as well as financial sectors, analysts said.

Meanwhile, investors remain cautious ahead of major events, including upcoming policy meetings of the Japanese and U.S. central banks.

data.title: Gold Rises Ahead Of US Inflation Data, Eyes US$4,500
data.description:
Gold prices rose on Thursday as a softer US dollar supported demand for the precious metal, while investors awaited US inflation data that could provide further clues on the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.

Spot gold rose 0.5% to US$4,423.81 an ounce as of 6.59am GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.2% to US$4,467.90.

The dollar remained subdued, making gold and other greenback-priced metals cheaper for investors holding other currencies.

Marex analyst Edward Meir said the weaker dollar was currently a more important driver for gold than geopolitical developments in the Persian Gulf.

“For now, ​the geopolitical developments in the Persian gulf are of secondary importance to ​gold. Gold instead is teeing off on a weaker dollar, which ⁠notably is not moving up despite the fact that U.S. rates are going higher,” he said.

Market attention is now turning to US producer price data due later on Thursday, followed by consumer inflation figures on Friday. The readings could influence expectations for the Fed’s interest-rate decisions.

Meanwhile, RHB Research said COMEX gold’s latest price action remained positive, with the commodity moving closer to the US$4,500 level.

The research house said COMEX gold opened at US$4,365.40 before falling to an intraday low of US$4,350.50, then climbing to a high of US$4,444.30 and closing at US$4,426.70.

RHB said the latest bullish candlestick suggested selling pressure had eased, while the 50-day simple moving average continued to provide downside support.

It maintained a positive trading bias as long as gold remains above the key US$4,300 support level, with US$4,500 identified as the immediate resistance, followed by US$4,700.

RHB advised traders to maintain the long position initiated at US$4,273.30, with a stop-loss at US$4,300. The next downside support is at US$4,150.

Gold also continues to receive support from concerns over US fiscal pressures. ANZ senior commodities strategist Daniel Hynes said confidence in the long-term value of US government debt and the dollar was being undermined by rising fiscal pressures.

The geopolitical backdrop remains volatile, with Iran saying it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the US sank five Iranian oil tankers.

Among other precious metals, spot silver rose 0.4% to US$67.52 an ounce, while platinum fell 0.8% to US$1,881.56 and palladium was unchanged at US$1,353.55.
